message.reasoning:
Let me evaluate against criteria.

C1 Introduction: mission concept (coral reef monitoring satellite), rationale (bleaching), number of spacecraft (one, justified), users — operator and customers? The intro says "operated and accessed from Australia ground facilities" but doesn't clearly identify operator and customers (marine/conservation scientists implied). Users partially addressed. References present. Adequate-to-accomplished. I'd say 7? Users not explicitly named (operator entity, customers). Some requirements addressed with detail. I'd give 6-7. The intro is detailed with references; users partially. Give 7 (Accomplished low) or 6 (Adequate high). Users requirement R3 is partial. I'll give 6.

C2 Mission design: launch (Vega E from Kourou, justified), orbit (SSO, 600 km, i=87.79°, elements table), maneuvers (only EOL), ground control (Mt Pleasant, STK access report), comms frequency (access table, ~20 min mean), mission duration 5 years, EOL drag sail. STK screenshots included (Images 1-5). Some technical errors: Kourou latitude stated as 45.05°N — actually ~5.2°N (likely typo, 5.05°? Actually Kourou is 5.2°N). "45.05°N" is wrong. Also claim "As this is smaller than the target inclination... two launch windows per day" — logic questionable. Inclination 87.79° for 600 km SSO: actual required inclination for SSO at 600 km is ~97.8° (retrograde). The plot shows inclination vs altitude rising from 96.5 at 200km to 99.5 at 1000km — that's correct for retrograde SSO. But the text says 87.79°, which contradicts the plot and the "retrograde" description. 87.79° is prograde, not retrograde, and wouldn't be sun-synchronous (needs ~97.8°). Major technical error. Also RAAN rate: says "1° east-ward precession every day" — actually RAAN regresses westward for SSO (nodal precession ~ -0.9856°/day, i.e., westward to follow the sun's eastward apparent motion... actually the sun moves eastward ~1°/day, so the node must precess eastward? For SSO, RAAN must precess eastward at ~1°/day to match the sun. Wait: the sun's right ascension increases ~1°/day eastward. For the orbit plane to track the sun, RAAN must increase eastward at ~0.9856°/day. J2 causes node regression: for prograde orbits (i<90°), node regresses westward; for retrograde (i>90°), node precesses eastward. So SSO retrograde orbits have eastward RAAN precession. The text says "1° east-ward precession every day" — correct. But inclination 87.79° is wrong; should be ~97.8°. The plot itself shows ~97.9 at 600 km. So the student read the plot wrong or typo. Also semi-major axis 7171 km correct. Eccentricity 0. RAAN 27.33°. Argument of latitude.

Also "an average contact duration of almost twenty minutes" — mean 580.786 sec ≈ 9.7 minutes, not 20. Error.

Also "very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable" — should be "not desirable" (typo). Also "which – because of its verticality – maintains a significant contact" garbled.

Also drag sail section: "It acts like a regular sail, utilising a large surface area to ' and is suitable" — incomplete sentence (conversion artefact possibly).

Also contradiction: "The proposed ZYZZsat is small and without thrusters... It would therefore make sense to choose an uncontrolled descent... However, the ZYZZsat is without thrust capability and so must use a 'passive' strategy." Redundant/contradictory.

Also graveyard orbit discussion irrelevant for LEO.

Also no appendix with STK files mentioned? Deliverable R10: screenshots yes; files — not mentioned explicitly. Screenshots present. Files not stated. Partial.

Also coverage: swath discussion, reef coverage. Ground station choice: Mt Pleasant at -42.6° latitude; near-polar orbit passes frequently — reasonable. But the claim "access frequency is maximised by selecting a ground facility close to the poles" — for near-polar orbit, high latitude stations get frequent passes; Tasmania is reasonable compromise.

C2 level: major requirements addressed with STK evidence, but with notable technical errors (inclination, latitude, contact duration). Adequate: 5-6. I'd give 5 given multiple errors, or 6. The design is fairly comprehensive with STK evidence. Errors: inclination 87.79 vs plot 97.9 — significant inconsistency; Kourou latitude 45.05 wrong; "twenty minutes" wrong. I'll give 5.

C3 Conclusion: summarizes findings, notes risks (Vega E not built). Some detail, somewhat generic. 6.

C4 Presentation: structure clear, headings, exec summary, figures labelled? Figures have captions like "STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart" but no figure numbers ("Figure 1"). Tables not numbered. References cited [1]-[10] in text and listed; Wikipedia used ([6]) which is not acceptable per task. Bibliography formatting poor (URLs only, no titles/access dates). Some grammar issues ("a Earth observation", "which is also desirable", "for the purposed of this satellite"). Adequate: 5.

Requirements:
R1 yes (Introduction).
R2 yes (one satellite, justified).
R3 partial (users implied: scientists; operator not explicitly named).
R4 yes (Kourou, Vega E).
R5 partial — orbit type and elements given but inclination value erroneous/inconsistent.
R6 yes (no maneuvers except EOL; stated).
R7 yes (Mt Pleasant, access table).
R8 yes (5 years, drag sail EOL).
R9 yes (STK used).
R10 partial (screenshots yes; STK files not explicitly provided/mentioned).
R11 partial (structure good, citations present but Wikipedia used, formatting issues).

Technical issues list: inclination error, Kourou latitude, contact duration misstatement, "also desirable" typo, graveyard orbit irrelevance, Wikipedia source, figure numbering.
